feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications/platform leader: the experience shows clear progression, relevant scope, and solid public-sector alignment. It is well written overall, but impact is diluted by dense text, repeated themes, and limited outcome-focused metrics beyond the website migration.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior positioning and specialization: the headline, summary, and experience consistently support a digital platform/governance leadership profile.  
- Strong career progression and credibility: long tenure at NACo with advancement across multiple roles signals trust, growth, and domain depth.  
- Good use of concrete tools and scale indicators: Drupal, GA4, BigQuery, 10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, and 50+ publishers add substance.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable outcomes across roles: include results for email, social, video, search, governance, and campaign work (e.g., engagement growth, efficiency gains, adoption, reduced publishing time).  
- Tighten structure and reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily; consolidate to create more space for achievements.  
- Fix minor style/consistency issues: “Coleman DAVIS” capitalization is visually inconsistent; punctuation in lists varies (e.g., “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma); “A2/Learning” is awkward—use “French (A2, currently learning).” No major spelling errors found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus, but it reads broad and repeats themes covered in Core Competencies and Work Experience. It would be stronger with one concrete scale signal and slightly tighter phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace “building the platforms” with more direct leadership language: “leading” or “delivering” enterprise platforms, governance, and content operations.
- Add one high-value scale cue from recent work, e.g., “10,000+ page Drupal migration” or “3.5M annual page views,” to increase impact.
- Tighten the second sentence by grouping related areas: web modernization, analytics, editorial governance, and AI-enabled discovery.
- Suggested rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience leading enterprise web platforms, governance models, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Delivers web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia programs, and AI-enabled discovery experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance models/content operations” and the long capability list overlap heavily with Core Competencies.
- “AI-enabled user experiences” is echoed in Recent Projects and Topline Skills; consider narrowing to “AI-enabled discovery/search.”
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block largely repeats the header and Topline Skills. It will be more effective if tightened, made more parallel in style, and focused on differentiating strengths rather than restating adjacent sections.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use shorter, sharper noun phrases and keep structure parallel; e.g., “Enterprise web modernization” instead of “Enterprise website modernization.”
- Replace broader items with more distinctive ones tied to recent work: “Drupal/CMS modernization,” “AI-enabled search,” “Analytics & dashboarding,” “Digital governance & editorial operations.”
- Consider a tighter version: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance & editorial operations • Analytics, dashboarding & reporting • AI-enabled search & content discovery • Workflow automation & platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production & livestream operations
- If space allows, add one technical differentiator not covered elsewhere, such as “CMS and content architecture.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” overlaps with the header and Topline Skills.
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” is already covered in Topline Skills and multiple roles.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads dense and repeats themes already covered in Work Experience. Tightening phrasing and emphasizing outcomes or scope will make it feel more additive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add dates or “Selected recent projects” framing to reinforce recency and distinguish this from core experience.
- Use parallel, tighter phrasing: start each item with a strong action + platform/output + purpose/outcome.
- Replace vague terms like “improve discovery” and “continued campaign growth” with clearer benefits if possible (for example, faster policy discovery, reusable campaign framework, expanded audience engagement).
- Standardize style: use “AI-powered” or “AI-enabled” consistently, and spell out “10 x 20-foot” for cleaner formatting.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search overlaps with the current freelance role bullet on “AI-enabled search initiative.”
- Advocacy Video Series and campaign/microsite items partially repeat NACo and freelance accomplishments in Work Experience.

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, competencies, and NACo entries. Make it sharper by emphasizing this engagement’s distinct consulting scope, technical depth, and any concrete outcomes.

Suggested edit
- Open with a clearer positioning line: “Embedded strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvements, campaign delivery, and AI-enabled content discovery.”
- Replace generic verbs (“support,” “advise”) with ownership verbs: led, architected, implemented, streamlined, launched.
- Consolidate bullets around 3 themes: platform/campaign builds, operations/governance, AI search initiative.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages/templates launched, workflow time reduced, search accuracy/engagement gains, stakeholder teams supported, traffic/member usage.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance, workflows, analytics, enterprise web improvement” repeats language already used in the summary, competencies, and NACo roles.
- The AI search and microsite work also appears in Recent Projects; keep this entry focused on leadership and business impact, not project detail.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics; it should be tightened to emphasize outcomes and distinguish strategic leadership from execution covered in earlier NACo roles. Focus this item on enterprise modernization, analytics, governance, and team leadership.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Rewrite bullets to foreground outcomes: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel leadership more specific: add email/social performance if available (subscriber growth, open rates, engagement, campaign results) instead of “tens of thousands” / “thousands.”
- Tighten ops bullets: “Built NACo’s first in-house broadcast studio…” and “Implemented GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery reporting to improve leadership visibility and decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Video programming and newsletter management overlap with the 2018–2022 role; keep this entry at the director/enterprise level.
- “Governance/publishing workflows” also appears elsewhere; frame here as organization-wide standards and cross-department operating model.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this item is too close to the Director role and earlier NACo role in phrasing. Make it more clearly about executional leadership, channel growth, and cross-team coordination before the later enterprise-scale remit.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + level: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, coordinating editorial and advocacy publishing across multiple internal teams.”
- Tighten bullets around distinct contributions: newsletters, advocacy video series, editorial calendar/processes, publishing workflow improvements.
- Add outcomes where possible: subscriber counts, open/click rates, video cadence/views, turnaround time, number of teams/stakeholders supported.
- Example rewrite: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and stakeholders; produced a recurring advocacy video update and improved cross-team editorial planning and digital publishing workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly advocacy video update” overlaps with the 2015–2018 role and Recent Projects; keep this version focused on scaling/adoption, not creation.
- “improved workflows/editorial coordination” overlaps with the Director role; avoid broad governance language here.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this topline item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent experience. Tighten it to emphasize senior leadership scope and distinctive strengths rather than broad communications phrases.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, higher-signal wording tied to current level:
- Enterprise digital strategy & web modernization
- Editorial governance, publishing systems & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership for public-sector organizations
- Audience-centered content strategy for advocacy and member engagement
- Consider dropping “messaging” in favor of “member engagement” or “content operations,” which better matches the CV’s demonstrated work.
- Keep each line noun-based and parallel; avoid vague phrasing like “audience-focused content planning.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” already appear almost verbatim in Core Competencies.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with the header and multiple NACo roles without adding a new differentiator.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities and group tools more strategically.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **Drupal and CMS modernization • Front-end web implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API and workflow integrations • Airtable-based operational systems • SharePoint and Power Pages • AI-enabled search experiences**
- Put **Drupal and CMS modernization** first, since recent roles and projects make this the strongest, most relevant platform signal.
- Replace generic “technical execution” phrasing with capability-led language; group coding skills into one phrase instead of listing each as a separate bullet.
- If possible, align with recent evidence by swapping in stronger specifics from current work, e.g. **Drupal microsite development**, **structured content workflows**, or **search/discovery implementation**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates much of **Technical + IT**; keep Topline Skills higher-level and save full tool inventory for the technical section.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies and the header summary.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for a senior digital leader, but it reads as a tool list rather than a value statement. It also overlaps heavily with “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT, so this section should emphasize strategic application over software names.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe as outcome-oriented capabilities, e.g. “Analytics strategy & reporting” rather than only listing tools.
- Tighten and group items: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity” then “KPI framework design, executive reporting, SEO/performance analysis.”
- Consider revised wording: “Analytics strategy & reporting — GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework design • Executive dashboards and leadership reporting • SEO and digital performance analysis”
- If you have metrics, connect this skill area to impact elsewhere (e.g. improved decision-making, reporting adoption, or optimization outcomes).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Nearly duplicates “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT; keep Topline Skills higher-level and leave full tool inventory to Technical + IT.
- “Leadership reporting” may be stronger as “executive reporting” or “executive dashboards.”

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it’s too generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value production leadership and event delivery rather than listing basic capabilities.

Suggested edit:
- Rename/reshape to stress scope: “Multimedia Production, Studio & Event Delivery”
- Replace generic bullets with sharper phrasing:
- Broadcast-quality video production and post-production
- Livestream and hybrid event production
- PTZ camera and studio system operation
- Virtual event workflows and technical run-of-show
- If accurate, add one stronger outcome-oriented phrase instead of a basic skill, e.g. “Built and operated in-house studio workflows for recurring advocacy and event programming”
- Keep this section at 3–4 bullets max; use Technical + IT for tools like Premiere Pro/Audition

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same wording here
- “Studio operations” and “PTZ camera systems” risk reading too tactical for a senior profile unless framed as production leadership or system buildout

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This item should either be tightened to emphasize strongest/recent platforms or add light context on level of use.

Suggested edit:
- Prioritize by recency/strength: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Better: **Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, group by depth: **Primary: Drupal, WordPress | Working knowledge: SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages**
- Keep naming consistent with the rest of the CV; avoid repeating broader phrases like “CMS modernization” here since that already appears elsewhere.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider removing one list or making this version more proficiency-based.
- Drupal is already strongly evidenced in recent roles, so avoid overexplaining it again here.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools that support recent Drupal, analytics, and automation work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename/refocus to: “Front-End & Technical Implementation”
- Rewrite as: “HTML5/CSS3 • JavaScript/jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions/CI workflows”
- Drop version numbers unless required; “HTML/CSS” is cleaner and more current.
- If accurate, add one higher-signal qualifier tied to recent work, e.g. “front-end troubleshooting,” “deployment workflows,” or “serverless scripting” instead of just listing tools.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” already appears under Topline Skills; keep it in one place or make this section more implementation-specific.
- “API integrations” and automation themes also overlap with Core Competencies and “Automation & Workflow Systems”; avoid repeating the same phrasing verbatim.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools**
- Tighten and group by function: **Automation:** Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | **Project/issue management:** Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | **Team collaboration:** Slack, Microsoft Teams
- If accurate, add a light impact cue in the section label or nearby summary, e.g. “used to support cross-team publishing, approvals, and communications workflows”
- Consider dropping one lower-value PM tool if not current/recent; prioritize platforms tied to recent consulting and director-level systems work

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same language verbatim
- Slack/Teams are common workplace tools; keep only if they materially support your systems/operations positioning

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as generic software inventory rather than evidence of email/engagement capability. Since email leadership already appears in recent NACo roles, this item should stay concise and tool-focused without repeating channel-management claims.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten platform names for readability and consistency: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add one capability layer instead of more tools: **campaign automation, newsletter operations, audience segmentation**
- Only keep platforms you’ve used meaningfully in recent roles; if one was light exposure, remove it to strengthen credibility

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding “email newsletters” or “multi-channel communications” here; that’s already covered in Work Experience and Core Competencies
- “Engagement” may overlap with Higher Logic/member comms, so don’t also repeat community/platform language elsewhere unless it’s a distinct skill area

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack, but this item is currently just a list and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” In a technical section, tighten it into clearer capability groupings and emphasize tools most supported by recent experience.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • SEO analysis • A/B testing • Executive dashboarding**
- Put the strongest, most recent tools first: GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Clarity.
- Replace generic **SEO** with **SEO analysis** and **Dashboarding** with **Executive dashboarding** or **KPI dashboarding** for sharper phrasing.
- If space allows elsewhere, move outcomes to experience bullets instead of here, e.g., analytics stack expansion, reporting improvements, or decision-making impact.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is nearly duplicated by **Topline Skills → Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider trimming one or making this section tools-only and the topline section capability-focused.
- “A/B testing” is fine, but only keep it if you can support it with examples in recent roles.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this reads broadly and overlaps with the 2018–2022 NACo role. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with clearer scope and any measurable outputs.

Suggested edit
- Reframe around early-team building and hands-on production: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team…”
- Add concrete outputs if available: website refresh scope, number/frequency of livestreams or weekly videos, audience/reach, email/social volume, or process improvements.
- Tighten phrasing and reduce overlap with later leadership roles: emphasize execution, production, and junior staff support rather than broader operational leadership.
- Possible rewrite: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team, improving production workflows across web, email, social and multimedia. Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates, while providing day-to-day direction to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 entry; distinguish this as launching/producing the series, while the later role focuses on expanding it.
- “strengthening workflows” is repeated elsewhere; specify what changed or what process was improved.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads generic and overlaps with later multimedia/digital roles. Emphasize coordination + launch ownership, and tighten the research/program support language.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the standout outcome: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo program and policy teams, while expanding digital storytelling and multimedia communications.”
- Make the podcast line sharper and more active: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- If accurate, add scope or output: number of projects supported, episodes produced, teams served, or audiences reached.
- Consider a two-part structure: research/program coordination first; digital/multimedia contribution second.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating broad “digital content production and multimedia materials” phrasing used in later NACo roles; this entry should show the origin point, not the full digital remit.
- “Overseeing planning, scripting, and production” is redundant with later production-heavy roles; “launched” already signals ownership.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it reads more like a mixed capability list than a clean tools section. It also overlaps with “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery,” so tighten it around software/platform proficiency and keep production capabilities elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Rename/reshape as a tools-first list: “Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator”
- If you want to keep non-software items, make them more specific and parallel: “Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator • Livestream production workflows • Podcast recording/editing”
- Consider adding level or context only if defensible: “used for in-house studio production, advocacy video series, and podcast launches”
